where: src/rl/rewards.ts:225-240 (waveCleared on waveIndex delta) + src/phases/attempt-run-phase.ts:51-57 + src/rl/phase-router.ts:998-1008
claim: waveCleared (+10) and bossWaveCleared (+25) are paid on ANY waveIndex advance, including a successful RUN: fleeing a wild battle pushes BattleEndPhase+NewBattlePhase, so the next decision snapshot shows waveIndex+1 and the agent collects +10 - 2 (ranAway) = +8 for a single safe action. The mask allows RUN in every wild, non-END, non-trapped, non-ME-blocked wave, and there is no boss gate, so even wild boss waves pay +25 - 2 = +23 on a lucky escape roll.
evidence: computeReward keys wave reward purely on postSnap.waveIndex > pre.waveIndex with no victory/flee gate; AttemptRunPhase on success destroys enemies without FaintPhase (no enemyFaints, verified faint-phase.ts:97 is the only increment) and pushes NewBattlePhase; ranAway = -2.0 vs waveCleared = +10.0 in DEFAULT_REWARD_CONFIG. Fighting a wave nets roughly +16 over ~5-10 decisions (~1.6-3/step with HP risk); fleeing nets +8 in one step with zero risk.
impact_on_learning: Flee-spam is the per-step-return-dominant policy for every fleeable wave: PPO should converge to running from all wild battles, never leveling, never catching, and only fighting forced trainer/ME waves — a degenerate policy that maximizes shaped return while learning almost no battle competence. This is the largest remaining reward hack after the shop livelock.
fix: Do not pay waveCleared when the wave was exited by fleeing (gate on lastFled, or on currentBattle victory/enemyFaints>0 bookkeeping taken pre-transition), or set ranAway <= -(waveCleared + margin) so flee is never net-positive.

where: src/rl/rewards.ts:61 (turnPenalty -0.01), src/rl/pokerogue_env.py:76,324-343 (NO_PROGRESS_LIMIT=40 truncation, no penalty), src/rl/cli.ts:330 (MAX_STEPS = maxWaves*50), src/rl/tunables.ts:16,38
claim: Truncation (livelock backstop, shop guard, step cap, wave cap) carries zero terminal penalty while losing costs runLost -50 (plus playerKo -5 each): stalling to truncation costs at most 40 * 0.01 = -0.4 (livelock path) or 2500 * 0.01 = -25 (full step-cap burn at waves=50), so a near-death agent's return-optimal move is to enter any repeated-observation loop and get truncated rather than fight and lose. The livelock guards bound the wasted steps but do not invert this ordering — they make the stall CHEAPER (truncation now arrives in 40 steps).
evidence: pokerogue_env.py livelock truncation returns (reward-as-is, terminated=False, truncated=True) with no penalty term; runLost=-50 fires only on terminated=True; turnPenalty=-0.01 means even the full 2500-step budget of a 50-wave run sums to -25 < |runLost|. The trained agent already discovered the shop no-progress instance of exactly this preference (documented in phase-router.ts:402-410).
impact_on_learning: The value function self-consistently learns V(near-death state) ~ 0 (stall+truncate+bootstrap) instead of ~ -50, so the agent is never pressured to avoid or fight out of losing positions; sample efficiency collapses because hopeless episodes end in 40-step no-op loops instead of informative losses, and the shop-livelock behavior will re-emerge in any other repeatable state (e.g. failed-run attempts, PP-less Struggle loops).
fix: Apply runLost (or a dedicated stallPenalty <= runLost) on livelock/step-cap truncation, and/or report those truncations as terminated so the -50 is learnable; alternatively raise turnPenalty so NO_PROGRESS_LIMIT * turnPenalty < runLost is impossible to prefer (would need -1.25/step, impractical — penalizing the truncation event directly is the right lever).

claim: The final (terminal) transition's shaping reward is entirely dropped: at game over, postSnap is replaced by lastSnapshot, which is the SAME object stored as calc.prevSnapshot in notePreAction (savePreActionSnapshot(this.lastSnapshot)), so pre==post and every delta component (hpDamageDealt/Taken, enemyKo, playerKo, waveCleared/bossWaveCleared, moneyGained, catches, stat/status shaping) is exactly zero. Terminal reward = runWon/runLost + fled + modifierTier + turnPenalty only.
evidence: episode-runtime.ts:171-172: notePreAction sets this.lastSnapshot = takeSnapshot() and passes the same reference to calc.savePreActionSnapshot(). rewardOnArrival:155 uses `terminal && this.lastSnapshot ? this.lastSnapshot : takeSnapshot()` as postSnap, then rewards.ts computeReward diffs prevSnapshot vs postSnap — identical objects at terminal. The scene is already post-reset at that point (comment at lines 118-123), so no true post-state exists to snapshot.
impact_on_learning: Systematic bias at episode boundaries: the run-winning action (killing the wave-200 boss) earns +100 runWon but NOT the ~+30 of shaping it would earn mid-run (bossWaveCleared +25, enemyKo +5, damage dealt); the run-losing action is not charged its playerKo (-5 per faint) or final damage taken beyond the -50 runLost. The same event is rewarded differently depending on whether it ends the episode, distorting the value of terminal-adjacent states relative to identical mid-episode states and slightly flattening the win/lose margin the advantage estimator sees on final steps. Asymmetric vs truncation: wave-cap episodes DO include full last-step shaping (cli.ts:643-651), so curriculum stages trained to a cap and stages reaching real game-over see inconsistent terminal reward semantics.
fix: Snapshot the true post-state at the moment game-over is detected (e.g. in the GameOverPhase intercept in phase-router, BEFORE the scene reset runs) and use that as postSnap for the terminal computeReward, instead of substituting the pre-action snapshot. Alternatively document that runWon/runLost are calibrated to include the missing shaping (and add the boss/KO components to the terminal bonus explicitly).

where: src/rl/rewards.ts:225-240 (waveCleared on wave delta) + src/phases/attempt-run-phase.ts:57 (successful run pushes NewBattlePhase) + src/rl/phase-router.ts:1006-1008 (RUN valid in all wild battles)
claim: Reward-hacking equilibrium: a successful RUN advances waveIndex (AttemptRunPhase pushes NewBattlePhase), so the next decision arrival pays waveCleared +10 while the flee penalty is only -2 — net ≈ +7.99 per fled wild wave with zero combat risk, no damage taken, no enemy contact. The waveCleared component does not distinguish 'cleared by combat' from 'skipped by fleeing'.
evidence: computeReward pays waveCleared purely on postSnap.waveIndex > pre.waveIndex (rewards.ts:225); fled adds ranAway=-2 (rewards.ts:248-250); both are attributed to the same RUN action at the next arrival (episode-runtime lastFled + wave delta in one transition). RUN is mask-valid in every non-trainer, non-END, non-trapped, non-ME battle (phase-router.ts:1006-1008) — the large majority of classic-mode waves.
impact_on_learning: Flee-spam is a strong, immediately discoverable local optimum: +8/wave guaranteed vs fighting (+10 +KO/damage shaping but with hpDamageTaken/playerKo downside risk under a weak early policy). PPO with dense shaping will plausibly lock onto RUN early; the long-term cost (no EXP, underleveled party dies at forced trainer/boss waves, -50) is many gamma-discounted steps away, and under short curriculum stages (waves: 10-20 caps recommended in TRAINING_SERVER.md) the episode truncates BEFORE the underleveling consequence materializes — the stage-1 policy that warm-starts later stages can be a flee-farmer. Warm-starting then poisons subsequent stages.
fix: Either (a) gate waveCleared on the wave being cleared by victory (e.g. require enemyFaints delta > 0 or check the transition was not initiated by ACTION_RUN — lastFled is already tracked, so: if fled, pay 0 wave reward or waveCleared*flee_discount), or (b) raise ranAway to >= waveCleared so fleeing is net-negative by default, and document the interaction in RewardConfig.

where: src/rl/cli.ts:580-581 (reward computed unconditionally per decision) vs cli.ts:630 (perspective only applied to the observation)
claim: In --enemy-controlled self-play mode, ENEMY_COMMAND decision steps receive the PLAYER-perspective reward stream: the single EpisodeRewardTracker computes hpDamageDealt=enemy-HP-lost etc. for every arrival, and the reward is attached to whichever decision arrives next — including enemy-perspective steps. Additionally, since a battle turn now spans two decisions (player COMMAND then ENEMY_COMMAND before resolution), the turn's entire outcome reward arrives at the decision AFTER the enemy's, i.e. is credited to the enemy's action in any single-stream learner.
evidence: runInteractiveEpisode computes `reward = tracker.rewardOnArrival(...)` at cli.ts:581 with no perspective branch; only buildGameState at cli.ts:630 switches to the 'enemy' perspective for ENEMY_COMMAND. rewards.ts has no perspective parameter at all. Commits 82e25dadc4b/d87f998fe47 added the enemy decision point and enemy observation but no reward mirroring.
impact_on_learning: Latent (PokeRogueEnv does not yet expose enemyControlled), but anyone wiring the flag for self-play training gets adversarially wrong credit: the enemy policy is rewarded for the player's damage output, and player turn outcomes are attributed to the interleaved enemy step — gradient signal for both sides is corrupted rather than zero-sum. Self-play training on this stream would actively teach the enemy to help the player.
fix: Before exposing enemy control to Python: negate (or perspective-swap) the reward on ENEMY_COMMAND arrivals, or maintain two trackers (one per perspective) and tag each state message with whose reward it carries; document that a shared single-stream reward is only valid when all decisions belong to one player.

where: src/rl/ability-features.ts:36-828 (155 of 311 ability rows are the shared default vector `D`)
claim: Half of all abilities (155/311) encode as one identical 40-dim default vector, and ability_id is not otherwise present in the observation, so those abilities are literally unobservable — including high-impact ones: SPEED_BOOST (line 44), SERENE_GRACE (145), TECHNICIAN (344), SHEER_FORCE (396), MOXIE (460).
evidence: grep count of `*/ D,` = 155; encodePokemonFromDict (spaces.ts:781-789) writes only the feature vectors, never the raw ability id. The 40-feature schema is 'FROZEN v1.0' and only covers immunities/multipliers/weather-setting families.
impact_on_learning: State aliasing: two positions differing only by a D-mapped ability are bitwise-identical observations, so the value function must average across them and the policy can never learn e.g. that a Speed Boost enemy out-scales it in 2 turns or that its own Moxie sweeper snowballs. Caps asymptotic policy quality on ~50% of the ability space; credit assignment for ability-driven swings lands on random correlates.
fix: Add a normalized ability_id scalar (or small learned-embedding index passed via info dict) per slot, or at minimum a has_unmodeled_ability flag + id/310 scalar; longer-term extend the feature schema for the top-N competitively relevant D-abilities.

claim: Level, computed-stat and wave normalizations saturate: getMaxExpLevel (battle-scene.ts:2105) gives cap ≈104 at wave 120 and ≈200 at wave 200, so `clamp(level/100)` is constant 1.0 for the final ~40% of a Classic run; computed stats exceed the /500 divisor for strong mons past ~level 150; in Endless mode level, stats, and wave all pin at 1.0 permanently.
evidence: baseLevel = (1 + w/2 + (w/25)^2)*1.2 → wave 120 ⇒ 100.8, wave 200 ⇒ 198. Stat formula ((2*base+IV)*level/100)+5 exceeds 500 at level ~170 for base-130 attackers, HP earlier. All three encodes hard-clamp to 1.
impact_on_learning: In exactly the run segment that decides episode outcome (waves 120-200, boss ramp) the agent cannot rank threats by level or raw stats — a level 110 and a level 190 enemy produce identical level/stat dims. Value estimates flatten late-run; Endless training is effectively blind to progression. Base_stats/255 and speed_rank partially compensate but ignore level scaling.
fix: Normalize level by the live cap (level/getMaxExpLevel) or log-scale; use log or cap-relative scaling for computed stats; log-scale wave for Endless.

where: src/rl/spaces.ts:1619-1651 (encodeDerivedFields speed ordering); acknowledged at src/rl/docs/SUFFICIENCY_MATRIX.md:21
claim: derived/speed_rank is raw stat × stage only — it ignores paralysis (×0.5), Tailwind (×2), Trick Room inversion, Unburden/Slow Start tags, and speed items, so it asserts the WRONG turn order precisely in the states where turn order is being manipulated.
evidence: Code multiplies stats[5] by STAGE_MULTIPLIERS[stage] and nothing else; trick_room_active is encoded elsewhere as a flag (spaces.ts:1031) but never inverts the rank; status one-hot carries paralysis but the rank doesn't use it.
impact_on_learning: A misleading derived feature is worse than a missing one: the cleanest 'who moves first' signal in the obs contradicts ground truth under paralysis/Tailwind/TR, so an agent that learns to trust it (it is correct in the majority of vanilla turns) systematically loses KO races in exactly the modified-speed games, and unlearning requires rediscovering the full interaction from raw flags — slow, high-variance credit assignment.
fix: Fold the known multipliers into the rank (paralysis, Tailwind arena tag, TR inversion are all already in the serialized dict); optionally emit both raw and effective ranks.

where: src/rl/spaces.ts:799-816 (volatile tags encoded as binary presence); src/rl/state-builder.ts:1239 (turn_count serialized but dropped)
claim: Non-Markov gap: battler-tag remaining durations are serialized (turn_count) but the encoder keeps only 0/1 presence — Perish Song count (3-2-1-faint), Encore/Taunt/Disable/Throat Chop remaining turns, partial-trap durations, and Slow Start countdown are unobservable, and the framework offers no recurrence or frame-stacking to recover them.
evidence: The 69 CURATED_VOLATILE_TAGS loop writes 1.0 per active tag_type only. Contrast: sleep_turns_remaining, toxic_turn_count, weather/terrain turns, and 5 key arena-tag turn counters ARE encoded — so the design clearly values durations, but per-mon tag durations were missed.
impact_on_learning: PERISH_SONG=1 for 'faints this turn' and 'three turns left' are identical states with wildly different values — the value function is forced to a blended estimate and the policy cannot time the switch-out; same for playing around Encore/Taunt expiry. This is aliasing on tactically decisive states; a feedforward policy provably cannot solve it.
fix: Add a turns-remaining scalar lane (clamped /8) for a curated duration-critical subset: PERISH_SONG, ENCORE, TAUNT, DISABLED, partial-trap family, SLOW_START.

claim: TM/move-teaching items are blind at purchase time: state-builder serializes the taught move's move_id for shop/reward options, but the 20-dim modifier feature vector encodes only tier magnitude (TM_COMMON 0.33 / TM_GREAT 0.67 / TM_ULTRA 1.0) — neither the move's type/power/category nor any party-compatibility signal reaches the observation.
evidence: encodeModifierFeatures dynamic slots are type_id/stat_id/status_effect/berry_type only; move_id is never read. All TMs of a tier are observation-identical regardless of whether they teach Earthquake or Splash-tier filler.
impact_on_learning: The agent cannot learn TM valuation — reward-picking and shop-buying gradients for TMs are pure noise, so it will converge to a fixed prior (always/never buy TMs by tier). Partially mitigated because the subsequent learn_move phase reveals the move's full 60-dim vector and allows declining, but money/reward-slot opportunity cost is already sunk.
fix: Use the serialized move_id to fill a compact move summary (type/18, power/250, category) in 3 spare feature dims, or add a per-slot 'any party member can learn' flag.

where: src/rl/rewards.ts:186-204 (position-indexed HP diff) + src/phases/switch-summon-phase.ts:182-183 (party array swap on switch, both sides)
claim: HP deltas are compared by party-slot index, but SwitchSummonPhase physically swaps party[slotIndex] and party[fieldIndex] for BOTH sides. Any same-wave switch between mons with unequal HP fabricates a positive delta in one slot: a player switching a 20%-HP lead for a 100%-HP bench mon is charged hpDamageTaken * 0.8 = -0.8 (as if hit for 80%), and an ENEMY trainer switch pays the agent spurious hpDamageDealt for free — farmable with phazing moves (Roar/Whirlwind/Dragon Tail) that force enemy swaps every turn.
evidence: computeReward diffs pre.playerHpRatios[i] - post.playerHpRatios[i] over the shared prefix with only-positive counting; snapshot() maps parties positionally (rewards.ts:133-140); switch-summon-phase.ts lines 182-183 reorder the underlying party array between the pre-action and post-action snapshots of a single step.
impact_on_learning: Baked-in anti-switch bias of up to -1.0 per switch (100x the turn penalty) teaches the agent to never switch — one of the core skills of the game — and every faint-replacement double-charges the death (playerKo -5 plus ~-1.0 spurious). Meanwhile trainer battles leak free positive reward on enemy switches, misattributing credit to whatever move the agent happened to use.
fix: Snapshot HP keyed by Pokemon id (Map<id, ratio>) and diff per-id instead of per-slot; ids are stable across swaps, catches (appended at end) and revives.

where: src/rl/rewards.ts:57 (moneyGained 0.01) + src/battle-scene.ts:2614-2621 (getWaveMoneyAmount) + src/modifier/modifier-type.ts:2052-2072 (Nugget x1, Big Nugget x2.5, Relic Gold x10)
claim: moneyGained = 0.01/unit against a money curve that grows super-linearly with wave: getWaveMoneyAmount ~ ((waveSet+~1.75)*100)^(1+0.005*waveSet). A single Relic Gold pick at wave 50 grants ~7700 money = +77 reward — 3x a boss-wave clear (25), ~15x an enemy KO, 77x a full HP bar of damage dealt, and comparable to winning the entire run (100). Even a common Nugget at wave 20 pays ~+3.9, more than a catch.
evidence: Wave-50 computation: waveSetIndex=4, base=(5+1.75)*100=675, 675^1.02 ~ 768, x10 (Relic Gold) = 7680 -> 0.01*7680 = +76.8. HP components are bounded at +-1.0 per mon per step; the intended 'money is a minor tiebreaker' scale only holds for the first ~10 waves.
impact_on_learning: Modifier selection gets hijacked toward money items over battle-relevant items (the item's actual value channel), and the return distribution becomes non-stationary with depth — late-episode +77 spikes dominate PPO's value-loss and advantage estimates, degrading credit assignment for everything else. Money income (Amulet Coin, Golden Punch, Happy Hour) compounds this since spending is never penalized (income-only accounting).
fix: Reward log(1+moneyDelta) or wave-normalized money (moneyDelta / getWaveMoneyAmount(1)), or drop the weight to ~0.001 with a per-step cap; keep spending unpenalized.

claim: Component inventory: hpDamageDealt +1.0/HP-ratio, hpDamageTaken -1.0, enemyKo +5, playerKo -5, waveCleared +10, bossWaveCleared +25, runWon +100, runLost -50, ranAway -2, moneyGained +0.01/unit, pokemonCaught +3, modifierSelected +0.5, modifierTierBonus +0.1*tier, turnPenalty -0.01/decision, statBoost/statusInfliction 0 (off). Over a 50-wave episode the shaping return is ~600-1500 (waves ~575, KOs ~300, money 100-500+), so the terminal signals are <10% of return — and under the default waves:50 cap, runWon (+100, requires wave 200) can NEVER fire: the only live terminal is runLost.
evidence: 50 waves = 45*10 + 5*25 = 575 wave reward alone; run_config.py documents truncation at the first decision of wave 51 with no bonus; victory in classic is wave 200.
impact_on_learning: PPO optimizes the shaping surrogate almost exclusively — fine if the shaping is aligned (RD1/RD3/RD4 show it is not everywhere), but it means run outcome is effectively not part of the objective in the current config, and the +100 runWon weight gives a false sense that winning is incentivized. Value scale ~1000 also makes the -0.01 turn penalty numerically invisible after advantage normalization.
fix: Either add a depth-proportional truncation bonus at the wave cap (so 'reached cap healthy' is the surrogate win) or scale terminal rewards to be meaningful vs cumulative shaping (e.g. runLost ~ -0.5*expected-remaining-shaping); document that runWon is dead under wave caps < 200.

where: src/rl/CHANGELOG.md:1004 (First trained agent table) vs :1020-1035 (audit round 2); models/README.md:5
claim: The documented headline eval (300.7 mean reward, mean wave 23.7 for ppo_v9_first) was measured under semantics the very next CHANGELOG entry admits were broken: --waves was a step cap (waves*50), not a wave cap, so 'waves: 20' episodes ran to wave 34; and truncated episodes handed sb3 a ZERO final observation during that checkpoint's training. models/README.md still advertises 300.7/23.7 without this caveat.
evidence: Mean wave 23.7 > the configured 20-wave budget is internally impossible under current code (env now truncates at the first decision of wave N+1). CHANGELOG audit-round-2 entry: 'eval reached wave 34 under waves=20' and 'the TimeLimit bootstrap used V(zeros) on every capped episode'. The smoke anchor was re-baselined (74 steps/50.74 -> 49 steps/101.83), confirming reward totals changed with the fix.
impact_on_learning: The flagship numbers are irreproducible with the current env and non-comparable to any future checkpoint: a policy evaluated today caps at ~wave 20, so mean wave and mean reward are structurally lower. Anyone benchmarking a new run against 300.7/23.7 will wrongly conclude regression. The checkpoint itself also trained with corrupted truncation bootstrapping (V(zeros) targets), so its value function is not representative of the current training pipeline.
fix: Re-run tools/eval_policy.py on ppo_v9_first under current semantics and replace the table in models/README.md and CHANGELOG (or annotate the old table as 'pre-wave-cap-fix, not comparable'). Retrain the baseline checkpoint under fixed semantics.

claim: Training is irreproducible: no seed is ever passed to MaskablePPO (torch weight init, action sampling, and minibatch shuffling are unseeded), and there is no --seed/train.seed knob for the learner. The elaborate per-worker env seed families are necessary but not sufficient.
evidence: grep shows the only seed in the trainer is the env game seed f"{cfg.seed or 'train'}-w{rank}". MaskablePPO(seed=...) is absent; set_random_seed is never called. Because PPO samples actions stochastically from an unseeded network, even the bitwise-deterministic env produces different trajectories every launch.
impact_on_learning: Two runs of `--config first_train.yaml` yield different models and different eval numbers, so ablations (reward weights, net_arch, fog_of_war) cannot be attributed to the change vs run-to-run noise. This directly undermines the branch's determinism campaign at the layer that actually produces the artifact being shipped (the checkpoint).
fix: Add train.seed to TRAIN_CONFIG_KEYS and pass it to MaskablePPO(seed=...); optionally torch.use_deterministic_algorithms for full reproducibility. Record num_envs in the run config (the documented run used 6 envs via CLI, which the yaml does not capture, and num_envs changes the seed families and data mixture).

where: examples/rl/train_maskable_ppo.py:119-133 (signal handler + finally) and examples/rl/first_train.yaml (no checkpoint_every)
claim: SIGTERM/SIGINT raise KeyboardInterrupt, which cleanly tears down workers (finally: env.close()) but never saves the model — model.save() only runs after learn() completes. first_train.yaml sets no checkpoint_every (default 0 = off), so the documented 200k run had zero intermediate checkpoints.
evidence: The try block is `model.learn(...); if save_path: model.save(...)` — a KeyboardInterrupt raised by the handler propagates out of learn(), skipping save, and the finally only closes the env. CheckpointCallback is gated on `ckpt_every and save_path`, and cfg.train.get("checkpoint_every", 0) yields 0 for first_train.yaml.
impact_on_learning: A preempted/killed training run (the exact scenario the handler exists for) loses 100% of learning progress at 199k/200k steps. On longer curriculum runs (TRAINING_SERVER.md) this silently discards hours of compute and makes 'train until killed' workflows impossible.
fix: In an except KeyboardInterrupt (or finally) branch, save to f"{save_path}.interrupted.zip" when save_path is set; give checkpoint_every a nonzero default in configs that set save.

claim: maxdamage is a weaker heuristic than its name implies: it picks max base power only — ignoring type effectiveness, STAB, and accuracy — and, via its ScriptedSkipPolicy fallback, it DECLINES every shop/free-reward pick, forgoing the game's main progression lever; 'Nx maxdamage' claims therefore overstate learned skill.
evidence: act() compares `move.get('power')` with a category!=STATUS filter — no effectiveness/accuracy/STAB terms exist anywhere in the file. Non-command phases fall to ScriptedSkipPolicy whose SKIP_PHASES includes 'modifier' and 'modifier_target', so it never takes even the free per-wave reward item. modifierSelected reward (0.5/pick, plus tier bonus) and all item-driven power scaling are structurally unavailable to it.
impact_on_learning: The trained agent's headline multiplier (3.8x reward, CHANGELOG:1410) is partly explained by the baseline refusing items, not by superior battling; progress reports calibrated against it will overestimate how much battle policy has actually been learned, and plateau detection against this baseline fires too late.
fix: Add effectiveness x power x accuracy scoring (type chart is already in the observation/state) and make the fallback take the free reward pick (skip only paid purchases), or add a second 'maxdamage+items' baseline so the item contribution is measurable.

claim: maxdamage is a weak baseline: it picks the highest base-power non-status move only — ignoring type effectiveness, STAB, accuracy, and PP economics — and inherits ScriptedSkipPolicy for everything else, meaning it DECLINES every shop purchase, never switches strategically, and never uses items. In PokéRogue, shop/item usage is a major progression driver.
evidence: act() reads only move.get("power") and category != STATUS; no type-chart lookup exists anywhere in the policy. Fallback is ScriptedSkipPolicy, whose SKIP_PHASES include 'modifier'/'modifier_target' — all shop rewards (modifierSelected, modifierTierBonus in rewards.ts) and item power are structurally denied to the baseline.
impact_on_learning: The '3.2x the scripted heuristic' claim overstates learned battle competence: a policy that merely learned 'buy something in the shop' and 'pick super-effective moves' clears this bar. Reporting against a baseline that is denied whole reward channels (modifierSelected, moneyGained via items) inflates perceived learning and can mask regressions in actual battle policy quality.
fix: Add an effectiveness-aware variant (power x type-multiplier from the obs or game_state) and give the heuristic a simple shop rule (e.g. buy the first affordable option); report both weak and strengthened baselines.

claim: Livelock truncations are misclassified as 'budget' outcomes: pokerogue_env.py:334-343 returns truncated=True with info["livelock_truncation"] (no protocol_error), and eval_policy's classification (error / win / loss-if-terminated / else budget) folds them into budget%, which is the de-facto success metric under a wave cap.
evidence: The env explicitly distinguishes livelock (NO_PROGRESS_LIMIT=40 repeated observations) from a wave-budget stop, but run_episode never reads info["livelock_truncation"]. A degenerate policy that loops no-ops at wave 3 for 40 decisions is truncated and scored as 'budget' — the same label as legitimately surviving all 20 waves.
impact_on_learning: budget% is inflated for pathological policies and the pathology itself is invisible in the eval table: a policy that learned to livelock (e.g. to avoid the risk of losing) would look like it 'reached the budget'. Since budget% is what distinguishes strong policies when win% is structurally 0 (see TE-9), this corrupts the primary comparison metric.
fix: In run_episode, record livelock = bool(info.get("livelock_truncation")) and report it as its own outcome/column, excluded from budget%.

claim: Truncation on the timeout/EOF/error paths returns an all-zeros observation with truncated=True and reward 0.0. Because SB3's VecEnv sets TimeLimit.truncated=True and terminal_observation=zeros for that step, MaskablePPO's bootstrap block (sb3_contrib/ppo_mask/ppo_mask.py:249-260, verified in installed 2.9.0) adds gamma*V(zeros) — the value of an out-of-distribution never-visited state — to that step's reward; the transition's true shaped reward is also silently dropped (0.0).
evidence: pokerogue_env.py:285 `obs = np.zeros(OBSERVATION_DIM, np.float32)` then `return obs, 0.0, False, True, info`; same zeros at line 309 when a done/error message lacks obsB64. stable_baselines3 2.9.0 dummy_vec_env.py:66-70 / subproc_vec_env.py:38-41 set TimeLimit.truncated and terminal_observation from the 5-tuple; ppo_mask.py:252-260 then does rewards[idx] += gamma * predict_values(terminal_obs). Contrast: the wave-cap path was explicitly fixed to carry the real final obs (cli.ts:550-553 capPayload comment: 'the learner's truncation bootstrap uses V(s_final), not V(zeros)') — the timeout/error paths were not.
impact_on_learning: Each flaky-worker truncation injects an arbitrary learned scalar V(0-vector) into the return of a random state, plus a lost final reward. Low frequency in healthy runs, but these events cluster under load (slow phases outlasting step_timeout), i.e. exactly on long/deep episodes, adding noise to value targets for late-game states. Bounded impact because occurrences are rare and gamma-scaled once.
fix: On the timeout path, return the LAST valid observation (self.last obs is reconstructible; keep a copy of the previous obs) instead of zeros so the bootstrap uses V(s_t-ish), or suppress bootstrapping by reporting terminated=True... simplest correct option: cache the last obs and return it with truncated=True; keep the zero mask for safety.

where: src/rl/rewards.ts:39-40 (turnPenalty docstring), examples/rl/train_maskable_ppo.py:97-106 (no gamma set), src/rl/docs/TRAINING_SERVER.md (no gamma/step-frequency section)
claim: Decision-frequency non-uniformity is real and completely undocumented: one agent step spans anywhere from zero game time (double-battle second command, SELECT_TARGET, each individual shop BUY, forced single-action EVOLUTION/FORM_CHANGE confirmations that surface mid-episode with a one-hot mask per phase-router.ts:816-825) to many game turns (auto-skipped sequences). turnPenalty (-0.01, documented as 'per-step time penalty') is charged per DECISION, not per game turn, and gamma (sb3 default 0.99, never set in the train stub) discounts per decision — so the effective per-game-turn discount and time penalty vary with menu depth and battle format.
evidence: computeReward adds turnPenalty unconditionally per call (rewards.ts:288); every state message = one gamma step in SB3. Doubles cost 2-3 decisions/turn (command+command+targets); a shop visit costs 1 reward pick + N buys + possible MODIFIER_TARGET steps; EVOLUTION mid-episode is a forced decision (mask with only action 0, phase-router.ts:816-830) that Python does NOT auto-play (pokerogue_env.py:64 SETUP_PHASES only covers title/select_gender/starter). grep over README/docs/examples finds zero mentions of gamma or discounting.
impact_on_learning: (a) Future rewards are discounted extra for every menu interaction in between — browsing the shop literally shrinks the value of the next wave by gamma^buys, biasing against fine-grained item play in doubles-heavy or shop-heavy configs; (b) with default gamma=0.99 (half-life ~69 decisions) and roughly 8-15 decisions/wave, the terminal +100/-50 is attenuated to near-zero beyond ~10-15 waves of lookahead, so training is driven almost entirely by dense shaping — a defensible design, but one the config/docs should state so users tuning runWon/runLost/waveCleared or wave caps understand what the agent can actually see; (c) turnPenalty is not a stalling penalty in game-time units as its docstring implies.
fix: Document in TRAINING_SERVER.md (curriculum section) and in RewardConfig: steps are DECISIONS not turns; recommend gamma per target horizon (e.g. gamma=0.999 for wave-50+ caps); note that EVOLUTION/FORM_CHANGE surface as forced single-action steps; optionally rename/clarify turnPenalty as decisionPenalty.

where: src/rl/docs/OBS_V9_LAYOUT.md:225-247 (§5 fog table); src/rl/spaces.ts:1555 (encodeDerivedFields takes no fog param)
claim: Full-info default is documented and the fog leaks (derived speed_ordering from true stats, unterastallized tera_type, ai_type) are explicitly tabled — but the mis-generalization consequences for a full-info-trained agent evaluated under fog are documented nowhere: (a) unseen enemy move blocks zero out, and full-info training taught the net that zeroed move blocks mean 'empty slot', so unrevealed enemies read as harmless; (b) enemy computed_stats/nature zero in the pokemon block while the leaked derived rank still asserts truth — a feature contradiction never present in training data; (c) indicator dims leave their constant training value (see OBS-L9).
evidence: §5 masking table marks the leaks 'documented'; no doc discusses train-full/eval-fog transfer; encodeDerivedFields reads raw dicts unconditionally so the regime mixing is real but at least deterministic and one-directional (leak, not noise).
impact_on_learning: Contained today because fog defaults OFF for both training and eval, but any user flipping fog_of_war=True for a 'human-comparable' benchmark will get a silently degraded, non-human-parity evaluation (leaks keep speed knowledge superhuman while move blindness is worse than a human's inference).
fix: Add a §5 paragraph: 'fog is a training-time choice, not an eval switch — do not evaluate full-info policies under fog'; optionally fog the derived speed inputs for consistency.

where: src/rl/docs/AUDIT_FINDINGS_P1.md:76-101 (v9 re-run: 44.7% raw per-slot deadness; 470/921 dead lanes = 21.8% of dims) vs src/rl/docs/WRITING_AN_AGENT.md:136 ('6991 normalized floats')
claim: Structural deadness is measured and internally documented (audit doc + dim-exercise-ledger classifies bench-structural: 15 dims × 8 bench slots = 120 always-zero dims, plus 12 move_effectiveness dims game-nulled before every decision point per ledger U8) but the user-facing agent-writing docs never mention that ~45% of per-slot dims are constant in practice or where the deadness map lives.
evidence: Ledger groups: bench stat_stages/damage_taken/acted/move_queue_len/other_tag_count/ability_suppressed/hit_count/wave_turn_count/is_terastallized all 'bench-structural'; active-slot/move_effectiveness 'structurally-constant' (turn_data nulled at MoveEffectPhase end — a dim that can NEVER carry signal yet occupies 12 slots). WRITING_AN_AGENT.md and README describe the vector without a deadness caveat.
impact_on_learning: Mostly wasted width/compute; concretely bites users who fit data-driven input normalization (zero-variance dims → divide-by-zero guards) or who assume move_effectiveness is a live feature and design around it. Not a training blocker.
fix: Link AUDIT_FINDINGS_P1 + the ledger from WRITING_AN_AGENT.md; consider deleting the structurally-constant move_effectiveness lane at the next layout rev.

claim: battle/money_log and battle/score_log are the only unclamped dims in the encoder — log(1+x)/log(100001) exceeds 1.0 whenever money or score passes 100,000 (routine in Endless, reachable in rich Classic runs) — and they are NOT in the invariants checker's >1 exception list, so the first rich run both violates the stated [0,1] feature contract and trips check_parity as a false positive.
evidence: No clamp() around either expression (every other scalar in the file is clamped); _GT1_PATTERNS contains only 'nature_mult', so feature_names 'battle/money_log'/'battle/score_log' get an expected range of (0,1).
impact_on_learning: Mild input-scale drift for the network (a money of 1M gives ~1.2, not catastrophic), but it silently breaks the normalization invariant downstream users rely on, and poisons the verification tooling exactly on long/Endless training runs where it matters.
fix: Clamp both to [0,1] (or raise the log base) and/or add them to _GT1_PATTERNS with an explicit bound.

where: src/rl/spaces.ts:1579-1598 (derived type_effectiveness: 2 players × 4 moves × 2 enemies only)
claim: Derived support is offense-only: the 16 type-effectiveness dims cover the player's moves vs enemies, but there is no enemy-move→player effectiveness, so 'expected damage TO US' (the key input for switch decisions and damage races) must be learned from raw type one-hots while outgoing damage gets precomputed help.
evidence: encodeDerivedFields iterates playerSlots' moves vs enemyTypes only; enemy move features are visible full-info (60-dim blocks) but effectiveness is left implicit. SUFFICIENCY_MATRIX.md:19 documents the derived chart's static-chart limitation but not the direction asymmetry.
impact_on_learning: Asymmetric shaping: early training gets a strong gradient toward offensive type-matching but none toward defensive matchup assessment — expect a learned bias to attack rather than switch, and slower acquisition of bench-matchup judgment (bench mons get no derived matchup dims at all).
fix: Mirror 16 dims for enemy moves vs player actives; optionally add per-bench-mon defensive effectiveness vs the active enemy's known move types.

claim: Several categorical variables are encoded as ordinal scalars, imposing false metric structure; species_id is the worst — adjacent dex numbers are unrelated species yet differ by 0.001, making species identity simultaneously misleading (spurious ordering) and effectively invisible (sub-noise resolution).
evidence: All are single clamp(value/N) writes on enum/ID values with no semantic ordering.
impact_on_learning: The network cannot use species_id to distinguish species (everything species-specific beyond stats/types/moves — learnsets, evolution potential relevant to Rare Candy/Evolution Item purchases — is unlearnable), while biome/status/weather-change scalars force the net to learn threshold decodings of arbitrary enum order, wasting capacity. Mostly compensated by the rich per-slot features, hence MIN.
fix: Drop species_id or expose it via info-dict for wrapper-side embedding; one-hot the small enums (status_effect in move vector, weather_change) as was already done elsewhere.

where: src/rl/ability-features.ts:30-33 (defaults [14-16]=0.333, [17-19]=1.0); src/rl/spaces.ts:772-776 (nature_mults raw 0.9-1.1); :936-939 (fog indicators constant 1 for enemies full-info); :844 (weight/1000); :1153 (pokeball counts /99)
claim: Near-constant / miscentered dim families: ~144 ability/passive baseline dims sit at 0.333/1.0 on every valid mon (duplicating the valid flag — the P1 audit's 'padding-locked' finding), 60 nature dims cluster at 1.0±0.1, 36 enemy revealed-indicator dims are constant 1.0 under the default full-info training regime, weight lives below 0.1 for most species, ball counts below ~0.15.
evidence: Default vector D used by 155 abilities carries those constants; invariants.py grants nature_mult a (0,1.25) range confirming raw encoding; OBS_V9_LAYOUT §5 table row 'indicators 267-272: constant (1 enemies / 0 players)'.
impact_on_learning: Constant inputs act as redundant bias terms (benign) but the constant-in-training fog indicators are worse: their weights receive no gradient constraint, so if fog is ever enabled at evaluation these dims move off 1.0 and inject arbitrary activations. Miscentered nature dims marginally slow conditioning. Minor throughput/width waste otherwise.
fix: Re-center defaults to 0 (encode deviations from neutral), encode (nature_mult-1)*5, and either train with occasional fog or zero the indicator dims when fog is off.

where: src/rl/rewards.ts:253-256,267-269 (positive-only money, tier bonus) + src/rl/phase-router.ts:1240-1263 (livelock sig includes money)
claim: Money spent is reward-free while the free reward pick pays modifierSelected 0.5 + 0.1*tier, so rerolling to fish for higher tiers has positive expected reward at a marginal cost of only turnPenalty -0.01 (reroll money cost is invisible to the reward). The shop livelock guard cannot stop it: every reroll changes money, changing the progress signature and resetting shopStuckCount. Bounded per shop only by the doubling reroll cost draining the wallet.
evidence: moneyDelta only added when > 0; getModifierTier pays on SELECT_REWARD; canReroll gates on money >= rerollCost (modifier-api.ts:134); sig = money|rewards|hpSum (phase-router.ts:1250).
impact_on_learning: Agent learns to burn its entire wallet on rerolls whenever offered commons — strategically terrible since money gates shop buys (potions/revives) whose value flows through HP components; wastes steps and couples badly with RD4's money-item bias (hoard money items, then torch the money on rerolls).
fix: Charge a small explicit reroll penalty (or price spent money at a fraction of moneyGained, e.g. -0.002/unit), keeping the asymmetry but not zero.

claim: delta_component itself is sound for monotone scalar accessors (wave, money, faint counters), but player_hp_fraction is a party-size-dependent MEAN: catching a low-HP mon or an ME party change moves the fraction with no health change, fabricating deltas for custom rewards (with only_positive=False, catching a 20%-HP mon into a healthy party of 1 reads as -0.4 'damage'). The only_positive=True default also reproduces the non-potential-based trap at the user layer: an HP-gain reward built from it pays revive/heal cycles (faint drop floored to 0, revive re-paid) — faint/revive oscillation farming with Revive Herbs whose cost is reward-free.
evidence: Mean over valid slots includes fainted mons at 0 and newly-caught mons at capture HP; the module's own docstring examples steer users to one-sided deltas; nothing in reward.py offers a potential-based helper.
impact_on_learning: Bring-your-own-reward users following the documented pattern inherit oscillation exploits and catch-penalizing artifacts, then attribute the resulting degenerate policies to their weights rather than the helper semantics.
fix: Add an hp-sum (not mean) accessor keyed to a fixed roster, a potential_component(phi, gamma) helper implementing gamma*phi(cur)-phi(prev), and a docstring warning that only_positive deltas on reversible quantities break policy invariance.

where: src/rl/rewards.ts:186-195 (only-positive enemy HP deltas, same wave)
claim: hpDamageDealt pays again for re-dealt HP after an enemy heals (Recover/Rest/Leftovers/boss regen): healing is never clawed back, so total payable damage per enemy is unbounded within a wave. With Golden Punch (DamageMoneyRewardModifier) each re-dealt hit also mints money reward. Rate ~+0.05-0.5/step, below the ~1.6-3/step of just clearing waves, so it is not the dominant policy — but it becomes attractive exactly when progressing is risky, compounding RD2's stall preference, and nothing stops it: HP/PP/turn-counter changes make every observation novel, so the Python no-progress backstop (seen-obs hash) never trips.
evidence: delta > 0 check only; no cumulative-damage tracking per enemy; NO_PROGRESS detection is exact-observation-repeat (pokerogue_env.py:328-333), which oscillating HP defeats; global budget is maxWaves*50 steps.
impact_on_learning: Mild positive drift toward stalling on self-healing enemies (notably bosses with healing) inflates episode length and injects low-value samples; with money-on-damage items it can locally out-earn progression.
fix: Track cumulative max damage per enemy id (pay only new-low HP), or penalize enemy healing symmetrically (making the component potential-based in enemy HP).

claim: Both shaped components reward one-sided positive STATE deltas, not potential-based shaping: stat stages reset to 0 on switch-out with no penalty, then re-boosting is re-paid (Swords Dance -> switch -> switch back -> Swords Dance = infinite +statBoostReward loop); enemy status cured (Lum, thaw, wave end) is free, re-inflicting is re-paid. The test suite explicitly codifies 'negative deltas contribute nothing', i.e. the oscillation exploit is by design. Defaults are 0 so this is inert as shipped, but it is the documented knob users are told to turn.
evidence: statDelta/statusDelta only counted when > 0; potential-based shaping requires the symmetric term (gamma*Phi(s') - Phi(s)) to preserve the optimal policy (Ng et al. 1999); switch-summon resets stat stages in game code.
impact_on_learning: Any user enabling these weights gets a policy-distorting shaping: boost/switch cycling and status/cure farming become positive-return loops, and the optimal policy under the shaped reward provably diverges from the unshaped one.
fix: Implement both as potential functions over the snapshot (reward = w * (postSum - preSum), signed), or document loudly that these must stay small relative to turnPenalty-per-cycle.

where: src/rl/episode-runtime.ts:118-157 (lastSnapshot reused as postSnap at terminal)
claim: At terminal the post-snapshot IS the pre-action snapshot (same object), so all deltas are zero: the killing blow that wins a run earns no hpDamageDealt/enemyKo/waveCleared, and the hit that loses it earns no playerKo — only runWon/runLost (+turnPenalty, fled, tier) pay. Necessary because the scene is post-reset at game over, but it systematically under-credits the final decision.
evidence: rewardOnArrival: postSnap = terminal && this.lastSnapshot ? this.lastSnapshot : takeSnapshot(); computeReward's pre is the identical object saved in notePreAction, so every diff is 0.
impact_on_learning: Slight credit misassignment concentrated on the most decisive actions of the episode; the final boss KO of a winning run is worth +100 instead of +100+25+5+damage, and the fatal mistake of a losing run is -50 instead of -55-damage. Mostly absorbed by the terminal magnitudes; matters more if terminal weights are retuned smaller.
fix: Capture a battle-end snapshot in a Phase.end hook (before scene reset) for the terminal diff, or fold nominal final-step components into runWon/runLost and document it.

claim: ranAway (-2) is charged for CHOOSING the RUN action, not for actually escaping: a failed escape roll (speed-based, probabilistic) still costs -2 on top of the free hit the enemy gets. Combined with RD1 this is exactly backwards — the failed attempt is over-penalized while the successful flee is under-penalized (net +8).
evidence: notePreAction sets fled from the executed action id before the escape roll resolves; computeReward adds config.ranAway whenever fled is true regardless of outcome.
impact_on_learning: Noisy, outcome-independent penalty on a stochastic action distorts the learned flee value both ways; once RD1 is fixed by gating waveCleared on non-flee exits, this attempt-vs-outcome mismatch will determine whether flee EV is computed correctly at all.
fix: Set fled from the actual battle-exit reason (e.g. detect the NewBattlePhase-after-AttemptRunPhase success path or check currentBattle victory bookkeeping) rather than the chosen action.

claim: Core PPO hyperparameters affecting horizon and exploration — gamma, gae_lambda, learning_rate, ent_coef, clip_range — are not exposed via the train config (TRAIN_CONFIG_KEYS covers only plumbing), so every run uses gamma=0.99 (effective horizon ~100 steps) regardless of wave budget; and the flagship checkpoint used the default 64x64 net that the script's own --net-arch help text calls 'undersized for the 6,991-dim observation'.
evidence: first_train.yaml's train: section has only timesteps/save; CHANGELOG confirms 'default 64x64 net'. A 64-unit first hidden layer bottlenecks 6,991 mostly-one-hot inputs to 64 features. For 50-wave+ curricula (episodes up to ~1000+ decisions), gamma=0.99 discounts rewards 500 steps ahead by ~0.007, but cannot be raised without editing the script.
impact_on_learning: Horizon-extension experiments (the stated next step in the CHANGELOG) will silently under-credit distant wave-clear rewards, and capacity is capped below what the input warrants; both failure modes look like 'the agent stopped improving' rather than a config limitation.
fix: Add gamma, gae_lambda, learning_rate, ent_coef to TRAIN_CONFIG_KEYS and forward them to the MaskablePPO constructor; set net_arch explicitly in shipped configs.

claim: On a step timeout during TRAINING, the env returns truncated=True with obs=zeros and reward 0.0; sb3's TimeLimit bootstrap then computes V(zero-vector) as the terminal value for that trajectory — a biased target for a state the network never legitimately sees (audit round 2 fixed this for budget truncation but the timeout path keeps zeros).
evidence: The code path builds np.zeros(OBSERVATION_DIM) and a zeroed mask; sb3 2.9.0 OnPolicyAlgorithm bootstraps truncated episodes from info["terminal_observation"]. Rare (only on 60s stalls/CLI death), so the damage is a trickle, not a flood.
impact_on_learning: Each timeout injects one corrupted value target and discards the tail of a (usually long, high-reward) episode, adding slight negative bias to value estimates for deep-wave states — the same states that matter most for horizon extension. Frequency is the mitigant; the env at least flags it via protocol_error.
fix: Cache the last real observation and return it (like the livelock path does) instead of zeros on timeout, so the bootstrap uses a real state.

claim: No dispersion beyond the median and no confidence intervals over N=10 (or 8) episodes, while the CHANGELOG draws cross-run conclusions (300.7 vs 285, 'didn't break learning') that are likely within sampling noise given observed variance (budget% 62%, best-episode wave 34 vs mean 19-24).
evidence: The summary prints mean/median/mean_wave/win%/budget%/err only; statistics.stdev is never computed. Outcome distributions are visibly heavy-tailed (retrain note: 8 seeds, budget% 62% means ~3 seeds died early), so the standard error of the mean reward at N=8-10 is plausibly tens of reward points — the same order as the differences being interpreted.
impact_on_learning: Hyperparameter or code-change decisions made from these tables (keep/revert) have high false-positive/negative rates; a genuine 10% regression is indistinguishable from seed luck.
fix: Print stdev and a bootstrap 95% CI per policy, and a paired per-seed difference (trained - baseline) which removes most seed variance; raise the default episode count for decision-making runs.

claim: The flagship config trains sb3's default 64x64 MLP on the 6,991-dim observation — a 109:1 compression in the first layer — despite the trainer's own --net-arch help text calling the default 'undersized'; the documented milestone run used it.
evidence: first_train.yaml's train: section sets only timesteps/save; policy_kwargs stays None so MlpPolicy uses net_arch [64,64] for both pi and vf; CHANGELOG:997 confirms 'default 64x64 net'. Observation features are hand-normalized to [0,1]/[-1,1] (observation.py _clamp usage, log-scaled money at line 2326), so scale is fine, but capacity is not.
impact_on_learning: A 64-unit bottleneck over ~7k inputs forces the value/policy nets to discard most of the carefully engineered observation (69 tag dims, 60-dim moves, bench encodings); learning plateaus attributable to capacity will be misattributed to reward design or observation quality in follow-up experiments.
fix: Set net_arch (e.g. 1024,512 as the help text suggests) in first_train.yaml so the reference config matches the framework's own guidance, and record it in the milestone methodology.

claim: Under any wave budget below 200, win% is structurally zero: info["victory"] is only set on a real game_over (classic-mode victory at wave 200), while a budget stop is truncated. The win% column is a dead metric in every documented eval, inviting misreading of 0% as 'never wins'.
evidence: pokerogue_env.py:522-523 sets victory only on game_over messages; a 20-wave run truncates before any victory is reachable. The documented milestone table omits win% entirely, confirming it carries no signal at this horizon.
impact_on_learning: Minor, but it means 'success' is silently redefined as budget% — which TE-7 shows is contaminated — with no metric capturing partial-horizon quality besides mean wave. Curriculum-scale comparisons at different wave budgets will produce win% columns that are incomparable across configs.
fix: Print 'win% (unreachable under waves<200)' or suppress the column when waves < 200; consider adding wave-N survival rate as the explicit success metric.

claim: info['invalid_action_count'] increments on EVERY warning-type protocol message, not only the invalid-action fallback warning — e.g. the CLI's 'Non-JSON line ignored' and 'Expected {action}' warnings (cli.ts:275-277) also count, inflating the metric that is documented as 'credit assignment was corrupted for those steps'.
evidence: pokerogue_env.py:466-468 `if msg.get('type') == 'warning': self._invalid_action_count += 1` with no message filtering; cli.ts emits at least three distinct warning texts.
impact_on_learning: No direct reward/gradient effect; it is a diagnostics-integrity issue — a user debugging mask/action desyncs via invalid_action_count can be sent chasing phantom credit-assignment corruption caused by benign protocol noise.
fix: Match on the warning text ('Invalid action') or add a structured warning code field to the CLI protocol and count only invalid-action fallbacks.

claim: keep_terminal=True adds the ENTIRE env terminal reward, which is not just the ±win/lose bonus as the docstring claims: per MDP-1 the terminal env reward also contains turnPenalty and, when the final action was RUN or a modifier pick, the fled (-2) / modifierSelected+tier components — these leak into the user's custom reward.
evidence: reward.py:170 docstring: 'ADD the env's terminal reward (the ±win/lose bonus)'; reward.py:212 `reward += float(env_reward)` adds the full scalar; episode-runtime.ts rewardOnArrival at terminal returns runWon/runLost + fled + tier + turnPenalty (deltas zero per MDP-1).
impact_on_learning: A custom-reward user opting into keep_terminal gets a small unrequested contamination (up to ~+1.0 from a final tier-5 modifier pick, -2 from a final flee, -0.01 turnPenalty) mixed into their objective; negligible next to ±100/50 but semantically wrong versus the documented contract.
fix: Reconstruct just the bonus from the env's reward config (runWon/runLost by info['victory']) instead of adding env_reward, or amend the docstring.

claim: Beyond the specific gaps in OBS-L4, no document states the Markov assumptions of the observation: which mechanics are duration-complete (sleep, toxic, weather, key arena tags — all encoded) vs memory-requiring (per-mon tag durations, charged-move identity via move_queue_len without move identity, Rollout/Fury Cutter ramp counters).
evidence: Docs grep returns only unrelated 'history' mentions; move_queue length is encoded (spaces.ts:887) but not which move is queued.
impact_on_learning: Users choosing between feedforward and recurrent policies have no guidance; a feedforward PPO baseline will silently plateau on the aliased states rather than fail loudly.
fix: Add a 'Markov properties' section to WRITING_AN_AGENT.md enumerating encoded durations and known gaps.

claim: arena.playerFaints resets on biome change; a player faint occurring in the same step window as a biome transition yields a negative counter delta (e.g. pre=3 old arena, post=1 new arena) and is silently un-penalized — at most one free death per biome transition (every ~10 waves).
evidence: RB2 comment acknowledges 'a biome-reset decrement is a negative delta and is ignored'; a decrement that nets negative masks a genuine +1 faint inside it.
impact_on_learning: Rare, small (-5) missed penalty; slight optimism bias for risky play on biome-boundary waves. Negligible unless playerKo weight is raised.
fix: Snapshot a run-cumulative faint counter (sum arena resets into a monotonic total in EpisodeRewardTracker) instead of the raw arena counter.

claim: Train/eval seed disjointness is enforced only by a docstring convention ('keep the prefix DISJOINT from training seeds'); nothing programmatically rejects --seed-prefix v9-train-1, which would silently evaluate on the exact training seed family.
evidence: The default 'eval-v9' happens to be disjoint from 'v9-train-1-w{rank}-ep{n}', so the documented table is clean, but the check is one typo away from evaluating in-distribution and reporting inflated numbers with no warning.
impact_on_learning: A future run with a copy-pasted prefix would produce a train-set eval indistinguishable in the output from a held-out one — classic silent leakage.
fix: Accept an optional --train-seed argument (or read it from --config) and assert no eval seed string is prefix-compatible with the training family; at minimum print both families side by side in the output header.
